summary: Post-market, the composite risk score rose to 42.88 (caution / goldilocks) with the 1-day trend turning positive at +0.37; all dimensions are fresh. The session was a rotation within tech: memory (+3.54%), gaming (+2.33%) and quantum computing (+1.50%) led, while cybersecurity (-2.63%), cloud computing (-2.31%) and AI software (-1.97%) fell; Broadcom (AVGO) dropped 6.13%, its biggest one-day fall in months, while AMD rose 5.31% on Tiger Global's Q2 build. Macro was mixed: the real rate at 2.42 (98.48 percentile) and the 10-year yield at 4.68 remain the binding constraint; retail sales missed, but disinflation held (CPI 3.30 / core 2.47). Breadth is not confirming: the new-highs ratio is just 3.23%.

top_risk_drivers.claim: Macro remains the binding constraint: the real rate at 2.42 (98.48 percentile) and the 10-year yield at 4.68 (97.51 percentile) keep the macro dimension at 62.02.
Breadth is not confirming: the new-highs ratio is just 3.23% (risk score 83.54) even as 70.97% of stocks hold above their 200-day average — leadership is narrowing.
The AI complex diverged sharply: Broadcom fell 6.13% (its biggest one-day drop in months) while memory (+3.54%) and Micron (+1.54%) stayed strong, and AMD rose 5.31% on Tiger Global's Q2 build.
The liquidity cushion is thin: the reverse-repo balance at 0.25 (risk score 97.75) is near empty and high-yield spreads at 2.71 are already tight; the Fed also unexpectedly paused RMP purchases.

supporting_signals.claim: The volatility dimension is the calmest (20.81): VIX at 14.63 and realized volatility at 13.37 support risk appetite.
Disinflation held: CPI 3.30 and core 2.47; the 10-year yield eased to 4.68 and the real rate to 2.42, with the dollar index softening to 119.06.
Cross-asset confirmation at 0.625, price 10.03% above its 200-day average and positive 3-month momentum keep the trend dimension from dragging.

contradicting_signals.claim: Labor data softened: nonfarm payrolls at -23.0 with unemployment at 4.1, contrasting with equity strength.
Retail sales missed expectations and the VIX ticked up to 14.63 from 14.55 — neither the consumer nor volatility offered a tailwind.
Crypto pulled back (BTC 62819, -0.85%; SOL 74.72, -1.73%) and the A-share semiconductor chain weakened (301308.sz -4.18%) — risk appetite is not broadening.
